items.prompt: Here is a picture fraction. It has five parts per whole unit.
Seven parts are counted, and so its symbol has a seven on top.
items.demo: *Seven* parts are counted, and so its symbol has a seven on top.

items.prompt: As more parts are counted… the number on top increases.
items.demo: As more parts are counted, the number on top *increases*.

items.prompt: As fewer parts are counted… the number on top decreases.
items.demo: As fewer parts are counted, the number on top *decreases*.

items.prompt: What happens to the number of counted parts as the top number increases?
What happens to the number of counted parts as the top number decreases?
Here are two fractions in symbol form. Which counts more parts? How do you know? 10/5  40/5
items.demo: *40/5*, because the top number is bigger.

items.prompt: Here are two fractions in symbol form. Which counts more parts? How do you know? 23/7  82/17
items.demo: *82/17*, because the top number is bigger.

items.prompt: Here are two fractions in symbol form. Which counts more parts? How do you know? 10/a  9/a
items.demo: *10/a* counts more parts, because the top number is bigger.

items.prompt: Here are five fractions in symbol form. Which fraction counts more parts? How do you know? 1/10  2/10  3/10  4/10  5/10
items.demo: *5/10* counts more parts, because the top number is bigger.

items.prompt: Here are three fractions in symbol form. The letter d represents the smallest number. The letter z represents the largest number. Which fraction counts the most parts? How do you know? x/10  d/10  z/10
items.demo: *z/10* counts the most parts, because z represents the largest number on top of the symbol.

items.prompt: Here are two fractions in symbol form. Which fraction counts the fewest number of parts? How do you know? 10/10  9/10
items.demo: *9/10* counts the fewest number of parts, because it has the smallest top number.
